Rashi on Nedarim 16a:10:1.hebrew: והא איכא נמי לתרוצי - בניחותא, דמשמע לישנא אחרינא: והאי דאמר "שבועה שלא אוכל", "דלא אכילנא" משמע, דהאי דאמר "לא אכילנא" בניחותא קאמר. אם כן לא להוי אסור, אי נמי כי אמר במתניתין "שבועה לא אוכל". אלא ודאי ליתא לטעמא דאביי, אלא ודאי תנא במסכת שבועות ד"שאוכל" — "דאכילנא" משמע ולא ענין אחר, ו"שלא אוכל" משמע "דלא אכילנא" ולא דבר אחר. הלכך מתרץ מתניתין "שאי אוכל", דכשאוכל ודאי לאו משמע, אלא אי אמר "דאכילנא":
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:10:1.english: And there is also [a way] to interpret [it] - [As a] straightforward [statement], so that it indicates another meaning: when he says, "An oath that I will not eat," it indicates "that I will not eat," for when he says "I will not eat," he says it as a straightforward [statement]. If so, he should not be forbidden, or even when he says in the Mishnah, "An oath I will not eat." Rather, Abaye's reason is certainly not [correct]; rather, the Tanna certainly [taught] in tractate Shevuot that "that I will eat" indicates "that I will eat" and no other meaning, and "that I will not eat" indicates "that I will not eat" and nothing else. Therefore, [the Gemara] explains the Mishnah [as reading] "that I will not eat" [she'i okhal], for [an expression] like "that I will eat" certainly does not indicate "no," rather [it applies only] if he says "that I will eat."

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:11:1.hebrew: זה חומר בשבועות מבנדרים - הא דאמרן, שבועה שלא אוכל כו', דבשבועות אסור ובנדרים מותר:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:11:1.english: This is a stringency of oaths over vows - [This refers to] that which we stated [earlier]: "An oath that I will not eat," etc., [teaching] that in [the case of] oaths it is forbidden, whereas in [the case of] vows it is permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:1:1.hebrew: מתניתין - דהכא לא קתני דלהוי מותר אלא הקרבן שאוכל, ולא קרבן שאוכל, ואהכי רבי מאיר היא ולא רבי יהודה:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:1:1.english: The Mishnah - [The Mishnah] here does not teach that [one] is permitted except [when he says], "HaKorban [the offering] that I will eat," and not [when he says], "Korban [an offering] that I will eat"; and therefore it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir and not Rabbi Yehudah.

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:2:1.english: Say the latter clause: "[Not] an offering, I will not eat of yours" — [it is] permitted. But didn't we learn - In the other chapter: "For an offering I will not eat of yours," etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:3:1.hebrew: הא דאמר לקרבן - אסור. ומתניתין דקתני מותר — דאמר "לא לקרבן", דמשמע: לא להוי קרבן מה שלא אוכל לך, דאם אוכל ליהוי קרבן; דהיינו מכלל לאו הן, ולית ליה לרבי מאיר מכלל לאו הן:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:3:1.english: That [case where] he said "for an offering" - [it is] forbidden. And our Mishnah, which teaches [that he is] permitted, [refers to one] who said "not for an offering," which implies: "Let what I do not eat of yours not be an offering," [implying] that if I do eat, let it be an offering; which is [inferring] a positive from a negative, and Rabbi Meir does not hold [the principle of inferring] a positive from a negative.

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:4:1.hebrew: שבועה לא אוכל לך כו' הא שבועה שאוכל אסור - כדמפרש בגמרא, דהאי שאוכל לא אוכל משמע; כלומר, שבועה תהא חלה עלי אם אוכל. והאי שבועה, ליכא למימר דחיי שבועה קאמר, דשבועה לית בה ממש כמו בקרבן, אלא שבועה ממש קאמר:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:4:1.english: An oath [that] I will not eat of yours, etc., [or] this [is] an oath that I will eat [of yours] — [it is] forbidden - As it explains in the Gemara, this [expression] "that I will eat" means "I will not eat" — that is to say, an oath shall take effect upon me if I eat. And [as for] this [word] "oath," one cannot say that he means "[by the] life of the oath," because an oath has no substance like a sacrifice [does]; rather, he means an actual oath.

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:4:2.hebrew: לא שבועה לא אוכל לך אסור - אפי' לרבי מאיר, דהכי גמרינן במסכת שבועות (דף לו.) דבשבועה אית ליה לר"מ מכלל לאו אתה שומע הן:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:4:2.english: Not an oath [that] I will not eat of yours, [it is] forbidden - Even according to Rabbi Meir, for so we learn in tractate Shevuot (36a), that regarding an oath, Rabbi Meir holds [that] from a negative [statement] you infer a positive [statement].

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:6:1.hebrew: שאוכל שתי לשונות משמע היו מסרבין - מפצירים שיאכל, ואמר אכילנא אכילנא, ומתוך כך אמר שבועה שאוכל — משמע דאכילנא קאמר:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:6:1.english: That I will eat indicates two expressions; they were importuning [him] - [They were] urging [him] to eat, and he said, "I will eat, I will eat," and as a result he said, "An oath that I will eat" — [this] indicates that he is saying, "I will eat."

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:6:2.hebrew: (כשלא היו מסרבין בו, אלא מעצמו אמר שבועה שאוכל):
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:6:2.english: ([This applies] when they were not importuning him, rather he said on his own, "An oath that I will eat.")

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:7:1.hebrew: רב אשי אומר - הא דקתני ״הא שבועה שאוכל״, ״שאי אוכל״ קתני, ולהכי אסור, ד״לא אכילנא״ הוא:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:7:1.english: Rav Ashi says - That which [it] teaches, "[This is] an oath that I will eat," it teaches "that I will not eat"; and therefore it is forbidden, for it means "I will not eat."

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:7:2.hebrew: פשיטא - דודאי אי קאמר שאי אוכל, ודאי לא אכילנא הוא ואסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:7:2.english: [It is] obvious - For certainly, if he says "she'i okhal," it certainly means "I will not eat," and it is forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:7:3.hebrew: מהו דתימא - האי דקאמר שאי אוכל, מיקם לישנא — כלומר, תקון הלשון — הוא, דבדעתו היה לומר שאוכל, ונתקל ואמר שאי אוכל, ונימא לעולם להוי כמאן דאמר שאוכל. קא משמע לן דלא, דודאי אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:7:3.english: Lest you say - [That] which he says "that I will not eat" is [a matter of] upholding the wording — that is to say, correcting the language — for his intention was to say "that I will eat," and he stumbled and said "that I will not eat," and [we] might say [that] he should actually be [treated] like one who said "that I will eat." [The Mishnah] teaches us that [it is] not [so], for he is certainly prohibited.

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:8:1.hebrew: אביי לא אמר כטעמא דרב אשי דלא קתני - במתני' שאי אוכל:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:8:1.english: Abaye did not state according to Rav Ashi's reason, as it does not teach - in the Mishnah, "that I will not eat."

Rashi on Nedarim 16a:9:1.hebrew: ורב אשי הוה נאדי - נדוד וסור מטעמיה דאביי, דכי היו מסרבין בו לאכול ואמר "לא אכילנא לא אכילנא", ותו אמר "שבועה" — בין אם אמר "שבועה שאוכל", בין אם אמר "שבועה שלא אוכל" — משמע דקאמר "אכילנא". אם אמר "שבועה שאוכל", משמע קאמר "אכילנא", דהכי קאמר בתמיה: "לא אכילנא, לא אכילנא?! שבועה שאוכל בודאי!" ואם אמר "שבועה שלא אוכל", הדין משמע נמי דאכילנא, דמשמע: "לא אכילנא?! שבועה אי לא אכילנא!" והיינו חדא לישנא:
Rashi on Nedarim 16a:9:1.english: And Rav Ashi was nadei - [Meaning] wandering and turning away from Abaye's reason, for when they were urging him to eat and he said, "I will not eat, I will not eat," and then he said, "An oath" — whether he said, "An oath that I will eat," or whether he said, "An oath that I will not eat" — it implies that he is saying, "I will eat." If he said, "An oath that I will eat," it implies he is saying, "I will eat," for this is what he is saying in astonishment: "I will not eat, I will not eat?! An oath that I will certainly eat!" And if he said, "An oath that I will not eat," this also implies that "I will eat," for it implies: "I will not eat?! An oath if I do not eat!" And this is one expression [of the two].

Tosafot on Nedarim 16a:11:1.hebrew: זה חומר בשבועות מבנדרים - ומפרש: "לא קרבן לא אוכל לך" וכו'. פריך בגמרא: דחומר מכלל דנדר הוא — מדקאמר "חומר בשבועו' מבנדרים", משמע הכי דהחומרא דנדרים אינה שוה לשבועה, אבל מ"מ נדר קל הוי — והא "מותר" קתני! ומשני: אסיפא דאידך קתני "שבועה שאיני ישן", דודאי בנדרים ליכא איסורא כ"א מדרבנן, כדאמר רבינא, וגבי שבועה איכא איסורא דאורייתא. וא"ת: לשנויא אחרינא דאוקימנא לעיל, כגון דאמר "קונם עיני בשינה היום" וכו', דלשם ודאי איכא איסורא דאורייתא, (וכי) היכא מיתרצנא לישנא דתני דחומר וכו' — דליכא למימר דקאי אסיפא, פי' כמו שמתרץ הספר, דהתם איכא איסורא דאורייתא בנדרים כמו בשבועות, כמו שפי'? וי"ל: דקאי אדיוק' דמתני', ונדקדק הכי: טעמא משום דאמר "קונם עיני", דהוי דבר שיש בו ממש, אבל "קונם שלא ישן" — ליכא איסורא דאורייתא כי אם מדרבנן, כדפרשינן לעיל דכולהו אמוראי מודו דאיכא איסורא דרבנן ולא פליגי אלא בלישנא דבל יחל. ועל זה אומר "זה חומר בשבועות מבנדרים", דבשבועות כה"ג איכא איסורא דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 16a:11:1.english: This is a stringency of oaths vis-à-vis vows - And [the Mishnah] specifies: "No korban, I will not eat of yours," etc. The Gemara asks: [The term] "stringency" implies that it is a [valid] vow — since it states "a stringency of oaths vis-à-vis vows," this implies that the stringency of vows is not equal to [that of] an oath, yet nonetheless a vow is [still] a lighter [prohibition] — but [the Mishnah] teaches "permitted"! And [the Gemara] answers: It is taught with regard to the latter clause of the other [Mishnah], "An oath that I will not sleep," for certainly in [the case of] vows there is no prohibition except by rabbinic law, as Ravina said, whereas regarding an oath there is a Torah prohibition. And if you ask: According to the other answer that we established above, such as where he said, "Konam my eyes to sleep today," etc., where there is certainly a Torah prohibition, how is the wording resolved where it teaches "that [this is] a stringency," etc. — for one cannot say that it refers to the latter clause, meaning as the text answers, since there [too] there is a Torah prohibition in vows just as in oaths, as explained [above]? And one can answer: That it refers to an inference from the Mishnah, and we infer thus: the reason is because he said "konam my eyes," which is something of substance, whereas [if he said] "konam that I will not sleep" — there is no Torah prohibition, only a rabbinic one, as we explained above that all the Amoraim agree that there is a rabbinic prohibition and only disagree regarding the [application of the] verse "he shall not profane [his word]." And concerning this it states, "This is a stringency of oaths vis-à-vis vows," for with oaths in such a case there is a Torah prohibition.

Tosafot on Nedarim 16a:4:1.hebrew: לא שבועה לא אוכל לך אסור - מטעם מכלל לאו וכו'. וא"ת: מאי שנא מקרבן? ויש לומר, דמשום דשבועה חמורה טפי מנדרים, משו"ה אזלינן לחומרא. עוד יש לומר, דטעמא דשבועה היינו משום דגזרינן שמא יאמר "שבועה לא אוכל" וידלג "לא", ובהא ודאי פשיטא; אבל גבי נדר, אפי' ידלג "לא" ויאמר "קרבן לא אוכל", ליכא איסור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 16a:4:1.english: Not an oath that I will not eat of yours, [the food] is forbidden - For the reason of "from the implication of a negative [one can infer a positive]," etc. And if you ask: How is this different from [a vow of] korban? One can say that because an oath is more stringent than vows, therefore we rule stringently. Alternatively, one can say that the reason for [the stringency in] an oath is because we decree [a prohibition] lest one say, "An oath that I will not eat," and skip [the word] "not," and in that [case] it is certainly obvious [that it is forbidden]; whereas with a vow, even if one skips "not" and says, "Korban that I will not eat," there is no prohibition.
